section_1.title: From ODEs to PDEs: The Leap in Complexity
section_1.content: Define Ordinary Differential Equations (ODEs) as functions of a single variable (e.g., time). Introduce PDEs as equations involving functions of multiple variables (space and time), focusing on how variables 'interact' in a multi-dimensional field.
section_1.example: Visualizing a ball thrown in the air (ODE) vs. the ripples on a pond caused by a stone (PDE).

section_2.title: Core Concept: The Heat Equation
section_2.content: Introduce the heat equation as a fundamental PDE. Use a 2D color-gradient grid to show how temperature diffuses over time. Explain that the rate of change in time equals the curvature (Laplacian) in space.
section_2.example: A cat sleeping on a metal plate; show the heat map spreading from the cat's body across the plate surface over 60 seconds.

section_3.title: Boundary and Initial Conditions: The 'Rules of the Game'
section_3.content: Explain that PDEs alone are insufficient; they need constraints. Use an animation of a vibrating guitar string fixed at both ends to illustrate Dirichlet boundary conditions (the fixed endpoints).
section_3.example: A robotic arm welding a seam; the PDE describes the heat, but the 'boundary conditions' are the physical edges of the metal sheet being welded.

section_4.title: The Big Picture: Why We Solve Them
section_4.content: Summarize that PDEs represent the language of nature (physics, fluid dynamics, electromagnetics). Conclude with a visual montage: weather forecasting, airplane wing design, and signal processing.
section_4.example: The flow of air over a bird's wing as it glides—PDEs allow us to simulate the lift and drag forces without building every single prototype.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Map to right side of screen: x from 1 to 6, y from 2.5 to -2.5
                x = 1.5 + j * 1.0
                y = 2.5 - i * 1.0
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "Boundary and Initial Conditions",
            [
                "PDEs require constraints to provide solutions.",

        rod = Line(start=self.grid["C2"], end=self.grid["C5"], color="#FFFFFF", stroke_width=8)
        left_fix = Dot(self.grid["C2"], color="#FFFFFF")
        right_fix = Dot(self.grid["C5"], color="#FFFFFF")

        self.play(FadeIn(rod_group))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF5733")
